questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The academic quality of the university, as well as the location (climate, language etc)

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy upon arrival, but somewhat difficult before. The student email was bombarded with lots of irrelevant information, så finding emails detailing deadlines was quite difficult.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The first few days had introductions and tours

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: International House was the only available venue for exchange students

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Housing cost included scaleable meal plans

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Campus housing is a bit expensive, but so is housing in San Diego generally. And the social opportunities are great!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: In general, the process was quite easy: Just click and add the course. The only annoying aspect was course requirements. Despite most courses requiring the same (2 years of study), you had to apply for each one individually, and for popular courses it was a bit of a problem

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: See above

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Aside from

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got everything I wanted, but I was also quite early, and quite lucky

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Allocate lots of time to studying requirements, deadlines etc.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were really well taught, but shorter

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was more interactive and intensive, with mandatory weekly assignments and midterms in addition to final exams. But the courses were shorter, so the overall course load was smaller.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Basically the mandatory 5th semester courses for political science, and then electives about international relations

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: POLI 122D (abuse of power) and POLI 143 (future conflicts)

questions.answer: Worth noting in the budget above is that the housing cost included 'dining credits', covering most of my food budget. In addition, I saved transportation cost by living on campus

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and housing was quite expensive. However, most course books could be borrowed at the university library, and a lot of services such as transportation, sports and cultural events had significant student discounts

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A free gym, athletic clubs (though some where quite expensive) and other social events

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The climbing club is pretty fun

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: San Fransisco!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easier than expected. There were quite a few distinct American features that took some getting used to. Getting to parties required somewhat of an effort, and the teaching methods are very different from Denmark, being more 'hands on' and interactive.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Living on campus is almost a must. While a bit more pricy, it's a great way of socializing. And since most exchange students live in the same area (International House), you also meet people from other parts of the world, giving you a good International network.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Probably the partying culture being more restricted (there are still opportunities though, they just need a bit of effort to find), and the courses being taught differently (though on the whole, they are somewhat easier).

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are very outgoing and easy to bond with. And the beaches are great!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Before the exchange: Don't underestimate the time needed for paperwork and other administrative stuff. Reach out to others going to the same institution, and coordinate when needed. And make sure to apply for I-house! 

And during: Make sure to reach out to as many students as possible, and allow time for social events. The stay will be an incredible experience, and will only become better, the larger your network is

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: See above

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The social life, definitely! Also, academics were great

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Honestly, the UCPH's bureaucracy. I might have been unlucky with covid confusing everybody, but there was almost no guidance, and lots and lots of nebulous rules that acutely needed streamlining. Significant improvement on that front is definitely required

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Nah

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
